description: The provided chart is a multi-layered donut chart illustrating the composition of “Analysis” as categorized in the MMAR benchmark, which evaluates deep reasoning across speech, audio, music, and their mixtures. The outermost ring, labeled “Analysis,” is divided into four major concentric layers: Perception Layer (40.4%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), and Signal Layer (4.3%). Each layer is further subdivided into specific analytical subcategories. The Perception Layer, in dark blue, includes Environmental Perception & Reasoning, Counting & Statistics, Music Theory, Correlation Analysis, Temporal Analysis, and Spatial Analysis. The Semantic Layer, in medium blue, encompasses Content Analysis, Speaker Analysis, and Emotion & Intention. The Cultural Layer, in light gray, contains Professional Knowl & Reasoning, Culture of Speaker, and Imagination. The smallest segment, the Signal Layer (4.3%), in very light blue, includes Acoustic Quality Analysis and Anomaly Detection. A small, unlabeled gray segment labeled “Aesthetic Analysis” appears to be an outlier or additional category, slightly separated from the main ring. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of Semantic and Perception layers, which together constitute over 80% of the analysis categories, while Signal and Cultural layers represent smaller but distinct components of the overall framework.
